{"sample_id": "blind-c8754bc887734b119045baf8b845399d", "theorem": "Prove that any two nonabelian groups of order 21 are isomorphic.", "assumptions": [], "domain": "abstract_algebra", "explicit_subgoals": [], "candidate_text": "Let G and H be arbitrary nonabelian groups of order 21.

By Sylow’s theorems, the number of Sylow 7-subgroups of G divides 3 and is congruent to 1 modulo 7, so it is 1. Thus G has a normal subgroup N=⟨b⟩ of order 7. Let A=⟨a⟩ be a subgroup of order 3. Since N∩A={e} and |N||A|=21, we have G=NA, and every element of G has a unique expression b^s a^r, where 0≤s<7 and 0≤r<3.

Conjugation by a induces an automorphism of N, so

a b a^{-1}=b^k

for some k∈{1,…,6}. Since a^3=e, we have k^3≡1 (mod 7). The solutions are k≡1,2,4 (mod 7). If k=1, then a commutes with b, and because G=⟨a,b⟩, G would be abelian. Hence k∈{2,4}.

Likewise, choose H’s normal Sylow 7-subgroup ⟨d⟩ and a Sylow 3-subgroup ⟨c⟩. Then

c d c^{-1}=d^ℓ

for some ℓ∈{2,4}. If ℓ=k, set x=c. If ℓ≠k, set x=c^{-1}. Since 2 and 4 are inverses modulo 7, in either case x has order 3 and

x d x^{-1}=d^k.

Every element of H has a unique expression d^s x^r with 0≤s<7 and 0≤r<3. Define

φ:G→H, φ(b^s a^r)=d^s x^r.

This is well-defined and bijective by uniqueness of the normal forms. Moreover,

(b^s a^r)(b^t a^u)=b^{s+k^r t}a^{r+u},

with exponents reduced modulo 7 and 3. The identical relation in H gives

(d^s x^r)(d^t x^u)=d^{s+k^r t}x^{r+u}.

Therefore φ preserves multiplication, so it is an isomorphism. Since G and H were arbitrary, any two nonabelian groups of order 21 are isomorphic."}
